name: ship_tiles
licence: the project's own generated geometry: no extract, no sample, no trace, no ODbL
rule: NES: 1 shared backdrop $0F, 4 background palettes of 3 entries, a 16x16 area carries at most 3 colours besides the backdrop, ten colours in the set; every pixel is a 2C02 output

geometry.tile: 16 x 16 px, the NES attribute area exactly, so one tile is one palette choice and the art cuts into four 8 x 8 pattern tiles without a repaint
geometry.plate_pitch: one plate per tile: a 1 px seam on the top and left edge means the seams line up across a run and the deck reads as plates rather than as a flat grey field
geometry.rivet_pitch: 4 px between rivets, so a plate shows four rivets a side at this size and no more; a real rivet pitch of 75 mm would be a third of a pixel
geometry.grating_pitch: 5 px: a 2 px bar and a 3 px hole, which is the smallest mesh that still reads as a hole at 16 px and keeps the holes square
geometry.bar_width: 2 px: one pixel of bar is a hairline at 3x and closes up on a TV; three pixels turns the grating into a solid plate
geometry.step: 3 px a step, four steps a tile: an adult's step is about 180 mm, so a 16 px tile is a little over two and a half metres of stair, and the tile is one storey-to-half-storey flight
geometry.ladder: rungs every 3 px, rails 2 px, which is the same rung pitch the stairs use so a climb looks like one piece of geometry seen two ways
geometry.hatch: a 14 px frame and a 10 px face: 2 px of frame is the only width at which a recess reads as a recess at this size, and the wheel is a 6 px cross so it is not mistaken for a bolt
geometry.rail: a 2 px bar and a 4 px post, both standing on the deck plate they guard: the rail is the edge of the ship, so the row below it is water and the class file says you cannot walk past it
geometry.water: a swell every 5 px and a glint every 6 px, offset 2 px between the two frames, so the sea moves without the pattern visibly scrolling
geometry.terminal: a 12 by 8 px screen with five text rows at 2 px pitch, and a 3 by 3 keypad: the row pitch is the smallest that draws a line of text as a line rather than as a smear

sources.card: the card's six families: plate steel, grating, hatch, bulkhead, the log terminal face, the water under the rail
sources.ship_row: data/maps/all.json, the ship_small row: 20 by 15 cells, tile_legend # wall, . floor, D door, H hatch, room_palette deck_day, story_flag ship_door_open (read only for this card)
sources.cabin_row: data/maps/all.json, the ship_cabin row: the wardroom door and the Percy battle, which is why the log terminal and the porthole have a face of their own
sources.spec: specs/15-env-tiles-ship.md: ten colours, three non backdrop colours per 16x16 area, water and porthole animated, the hatch open and closed told apart at a glance, solids on the tile
sources.palette: tools/art/make_env_ship.py PALETTE, lines 61 to 72: the ship strip's own ten 2C02 entries
sources.quay: game/sprites_src/env/quay/TILES.md: the exterior set the player walks in from, so the sea and the stone are the ones this deck is moored beside
sources.geometry: generated: no extract, no sample, no trace; every number is in GEOMETRY above

k.why: backdrop: the hatch void, seams, the drop beyond the rail

m.why: steel mid: deck plates, the bulkhead face, the opening in a plate

l.why: steel light: lit plate edges, rails, rivets, ladder stringers

w.why: white paint: the walkway line, lamp glass, foam on a crest

a.why: sea deep: the water under the rail

b.why: sea mid: one step of swell above the deep

c.why: sea crest and the terminal's screen

r.why: rust dark: the shadow under a bar, risers, the warm dark in a joint

o.why: rust: pipe bodies, the terminal bezel, the dark side of the brass

y.why: brass and hazard yellow: the porthole ring, the keypad, the stripes

palettes.name: bg0_deck
palettes.note: the deck itself and everything painted on it: plate, line, hatch, sill, lamp

palettes.name: bg1_hold
palettes.note: the hold's ironwork: grating, bulkhead, ladder, stairs, pipes, locker, crate, the rail

palettes.name: bg2_sea
palettes.note: the water under the rail: deep, swell, the crest and the foam at the hull

palettes.name: bg3_fixture
palettes.note: the things that are read rather than walked on: hazard paint, the porthole, the log terminal

tiles.name: deck_plate
tiles.note: a plate of the deck: one plate a tile, seam on two edges, four rivets
tiles.walk_reason: a deck plate is the floor the fight happens on

tiles.name: deck_plate_worn
tiles.note: the same plate with tread scuffs, so a long deck is not one tile repeated
tiles.walk_reason: a deck plate is the floor the fight happens on

tiles.name: deck_line
tiles.note: the painted walkway line, two pixels wide, along the plate
tiles.walk_reason: paint on a deck plate: it does not stop a step

tiles.name: deck_grating
tiles.note: open steel grating: a two pixel bar and a three pixel hole
tiles.walk_reason: grating is walked on; the engine space and the catwalk are laid in it

tiles.name: deck_grating_cross
tiles.note: the grating with a raised centre member over it
tiles.walk_reason: grating is walked on, and the member is flush enough to step over

tiles.name: hatch_closed
tiles.note: a closed deck hatch: frame, recessed face, the wheel
tiles.walk_reason: a shut hatch is a solid: the map blocks it, and it is the blocked until story flag cell

tiles.name: hatch_open
tiles.note: the same hatch swung open: the void below and the tops of its ladder
tiles.walk_reason: an open hatch is the way down: walkable, and it is the cell the ladder_down trigger sits on

tiles.name: door_sill
tiles.note: the sill across a watertight doorway, worn to the steel
tiles.walk_reason: a sill is a step of two pixels: crossable, so the map does not block it

tiles.name: bulkhead_rivet
tiles.note: a riveted bulkhead: plate seam, a four by four rivet grid, dark base course
tiles.walk_reason: a bulkhead is a wall

tiles.name: bulkhead_plain
tiles.note: the same bulkhead with no rivets, lit along its top edge
tiles.walk_reason: a bulkhead is a wall

tiles.name: bulkhead_light
tiles.note: a bulkhead lamp and the first row of its spill
tiles.walk_reason: a fitting on a wall: it is not ground

tiles.name: ladder
tiles.note: a vertical ladder: two stringers, rungs every three pixels
tiles.walk_reason: a ladder is climbed, not walked around; the map lets a step onto it

tiles.name: stairs_up
tiles.note: a short stair up to the weather deck, four treads
tiles.walk_reason: a stair is climbed, so it is not a solid

tiles.name: pipe_run
tiles.note: a pipe run along a bulkhead, with two flanges and a lagging line
tiles.walk_reason: a pipe run stands proud of the wall: a solid

tiles.name: locker
tiles.note: a steel locker: louvred door, handle, dark base
tiles.walk_reason: a locker is furniture: a solid

tiles.name: crate
tiles.note: a crate in the hold, banded with a diagonal brace
tiles.walk_reason: a crate is a solid the hold is furnished with

tiles.name: hazard_stripes
tiles.note: hazard paint: a yellow field, black diagonal stripes, rust at its edge
tiles.walk_reason: paint on a deck: it marks a hazard, it is not one

tiles.name: rail_post
tiles.note: a rail stanchion standing on the deck plate it guards
tiles.walk_reason: the rail is the edge of the ship: a solid, and the deck ends at it

tiles.name: rail_bar
tiles.note: the rail bar and its shadow, on the deck plate at the ship's edge, with the water beyond
tiles.walk_reason: the rail is the edge of the ship: a solid, and the water is under it

tiles.name: porthole
tiles.note: a brass porthole: ring, glass, the harbour showing through it
tiles.walk_reason: a porthole is set in a bulkhead: a solid

tiles.name: log_terminal
tiles.note: the log terminal face: screen with five text rows, keypad, one live indicator
tiles.walk_reason: a terminal is mounted on a wall: it is the save point, not ground

tiles.name: water_deep
tiles.note: the water under the rail, frame 1 of 2: deep blue, two swells, three glints
tiles.walk_reason: you cannot walk on the sea

tiles.name: water_swell
tiles.note: the water under the rail, frame 2 of 2: the swell moves two pixels and the glints swap
tiles.walk_reason: you cannot walk on the sea

tiles.name: water_edge
tiles.note: the waterline at the hull: crest against the steel, foam breaking
tiles.walk_reason: the waterline is water: the hull beside it is a solid too

animation.note: the sea under the rail: two frames, the swell moves two pixels

hatch.rule: the closed hatch is not walkable and is the flag gated cell (collision 2 in the data/maps/all.json convention); the open hatch is walkable and carries the ladder_down trigger

rail.rule: the rail is the edge of the ship: not walkable, stood on the deck plate it guards, with the water in the next row below it
